system_description.narrative_title: Global bond yield surge and sovereign stress
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid, broad-based rise in government bond yields is disrupting capital markets, repricing risk across sovereigns, banks and equities. The move has amplified fiscal stress in vulnerable countries—most visibly France—forced changes in debt issuance strategy, and prompted intense market attention to auctions and central-bank communication. Spillovers to bank shares, corporate credit and investor retirement portfolios are driving policy and market responses that will determine whether the episode stabilizes or evolves into a broader financial-fragility loop.
system_description.scope: Sovereign and corporate bond markets (yields, spreads, auctions), central-bank policy and communications, sovereign fiscal positions and debt issuance strategies (notably France), banking-sector credit risk, equity-market valuation effects, and investor flows/asset-allocation decisions.
system_description.super_system: Global financial and macroeconomic system (capital markets, central banks, sovereign fiscal policy, global institutional and retail investors)
adjacent_subsystems: Domestic fiscal politics and public finances (e.g., France's budget and political reactions)
Banking-sector stability and interbank credit markets
Equities and institutional investor risk allocation

variables.name: Government bond yield level
variables.description: The prevailing nominal yield on sovereign fixed-income instruments aggregated across the market.

variables.name: Sovereign credit spread level
variables.description: The average market premium demanded over benchmark yields to hold sovereign debt reflecting perceived sovereign credit risk.

variables.name: Term premium level
variables.description: The component of long-term government yields that compensates investors for interest-rate and reinvestment risk over the term.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The ease and depth with which government and corporate bonds can be transacted without large price impact.

variables.name: Bond yield volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term fluctuation intensity of yields in the sovereign and corporate bond markets.

variables.name: Sovereign debt maturity profile
variables.description: The distribution of outstanding sovereign liabilities across remaining time-to-maturity buckets.

variables.name: Sovereign debt-to-GDP ratio
variables.description: The stock of public sector debt measured relative to the size of the domestic economy.

variables.name: Sovereign fiscal deficit flow
variables.description: The ongoing net borrowing requirement of the public sector measured per period.

variables.name: Policy interest rate level
variables.description: The prevailing short-term policy interest rate set by monetary authorities as the anchor for market rates.

variables.name: Central-bank communication credibility
variables.description: The market perception of how reliably central-bank statements and forward guidance influence future policy and outcomes.

variables.name: Primary market auction demand
variables.description: The level of investor demand for newly issued sovereign bonds at primary auctions relative to supply.

variables.name: Banking-sector funding stress
variables.description: The pressure on financial intermediaries to obtain short- and long-term funding, reflected in funding spreads and roll-over costs.

variables.name: Corporate credit spread level
variables.description: The average premium corporate borrowers pay over risk-free yields, reflecting corporate default and liquidity risk.

variables.name: Equity market valuation level
variables.description: The aggregate valuation metric for equity markets (e.g., price-to-earnings or market-to-GDP) that determines price sensitivity to yield moves.

variables.name: Investor fixed‑income allocation
variables.description: The share of investable assets allocated to fixed‑income instruments across institutional and retail investor portfolios.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flow
variables.description: The net movement of capital into or out of domestic bond and equity markets from foreign investors per period.

catalysts.title: Upcoming US Treasury auctions (investor vote)
catalysts.description: A sequence of near-term US Treasury auctions will act as a test of investor confidence and likely move yields and liquidity.
catalysts.rationale: “The Treasury market is facing a crucial vote of investor confidence”; “Auction Action Calms Treasurys”.

catalysts.title: Eurozone ministers push France to pass 2027 budget
catalysts.description: Eurozone ministers pressing France to pass the 2027 budget aims to calm markets and could compress French spreads if enacted.
catalysts.rationale: “Euro zone ministers to tell France to pass 2027 budget to calm markets.”

catalysts.title: French government may bypass parliament to push cuts
catalysts.description: Paris's willingness to bypass parliament to pass large spending cuts could materially change near-term fiscal flows and market risk pricing.
catalysts.rationale: “Exclusive | French Government Is Willing to Bypass Parliament to Pass Billions in Cuts.”

catalysts.title: France considers issuing more shorter‑term debt
catalysts.description: Shift toward shorter-term issuance after market turmoil would alter maturity structure and primary demand dynamics, affecting short-term funding needs.
catalysts.rationale: “Exclusive | France Considers Issuing More Shorter-Term Debt After Bond-Market Turmoil.”

catalysts.title: Steps to replace ECB's Schnabel (governance change)
catalysts.description: Finance ministers initiating replacement steps for ECB policy member Schnabel could change central-bank communications and market confidence.
catalysts.rationale: “Euro zone finance ministers start steps to replace ECB's Schnabel.”

catalysts.title: Continuation of global bond sell‑off
catalysts.description: Ongoing global bond sell-off momentum could further raise yields, widen spreads and amplify volatility and bank funding pressures in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: “US bonds selloff resumes…10-year, 30-yields hit new 24-year high”; “European bank shares fall as bond yields surge.”
